findings.label: M-01
findings.title: MEV / first-claimer front-run of winner-take-all nudge pot
findings.note: NEW at run phoenix-nft-staking-13. Distinct root cause from H-01 (mempool race vs. value-blind gate). Report generated and PoC (poc-MevFrontrunNudge.t.sol) validated passing; moved to submitted. [TRIAGE 2026-05-29] Accepted — valid finding. Mitigation: introduce a `minRewardPayout` parameter so the claimer can use AMM-style slippage mechanics to revert the transaction if their expected reward has been front-run/claimed. This protects an honest batch-minter from spending a large sum and receiving nothing. [TRIAGE 2026-05-30] ACCEPTED as residual (user triage 2026-05-30). Threat model verified against batchMint @ 9be4a87: (cond.2) claiming the nudge requires paying nudgeSize×mintPrice for real mints — the owner-pinned minter/dispatcher (story-009) make a free claim impossible (verified L257-259, L270); (cond.1) the minReward floor (L278-279) reverts the loser's batch atomically so a sniped user never overpays for a gone reward. Winner-take-all MEV capture remains by design and is accepted: nudge reward is a fraction of NFT mint cost, NFTs have no secondary market (only the staking pool), so a pure MEV bot cannot recoup in one tx — a front-runner who claims must genuinely join the protocol, reducing the issue to an ordinary gas auction among real participants. ACCEPTANCE INVARIANT (owner-operational, not code-enforced): keep the nudge pot < nudgeSize×mintPrice; if the yield funnel ever lets the pot exceed the cost of nudgeSize mints, pure-profit MEV returns. Also assumes a non-zero dispatcher mint price when the nudge is funded. [phoenix-nft-staking-16 RE-TRIAGE] The acceptance invariant 'keep pot < nudgeSize x mintPrice' does NOT bound loss if the minted NFTs carry realizable (resellable/redeemable) value: a searcher who realizes NFT value nets ~pot>0 for ANY pot size, so the giveaway is raced to zero on every refill — the 'NFTs have no secondary market' premise of the 2026-05-30 acceptance no longer holds if a market/redemption path exists (RETRIAGE-001 / ECON-002 / cross-ref F-01 lineage). Over-funding facet (PATTERN-002) is a non-obvious Law-3 owner footgun ('fund the incentive' silently == 'set a sweepable bounty'). Severity ceiling RE-CONFIRMED MEDIUM (NOT secretly High: no principal theft, honest minters still receive NFTs and story-015 minReward reverts a sniped honest caller atomically; loss bounded by owner funding; mempool ordering race, not an unconditional drain). [FIXED 2026-06-09] The core actionable harm was honest-user overpayment: a caller pays nudgeSize×mintPrice expecting a reward and receives nothing. This is fully closed by the `minReward` slippage floor (story-015): if the pot has been front-run, the batch reverts atomically and the honest user pays nothing. The remaining race — who wins the pot among qualifying batches — is an accepted gas-auction among genuine protocol participants, each of whom must pay the full mint cost. `nudgeSize` ensures no free-claim path exists (story-009). Marked fixed at HEAD 5f863d27 per owner triage 2026-06-09. [phoenix-nft-staking-20] ⚠ EXPIRED-CLOSURE — REOPEN PROPOSED at Medium (severity assessed AT HEAD, historical label given no weight). STATUS NOT FLIPPED (D-09). ⚠ THIS ENTRY CARRIES AN OWNER-SIGNED 2026-06-09 TRIAGE, so it needs the operator's eyes most. INVALID CLOSURE, **NOT A CODE REGRESSION** — no path got worse; P1 still holds. The four premises the `fixed` rests on, re-tested at HEAD: P1 'free claim impossible' HOLDS ✅ (owner-pinned minter/dispatcher). P2 'pot below mint cost' ✗ DEGRADED/UNENFORCED AND SELF-TRIGGERING — the entry states its own trigger ('if the yield funnel ever lets the pot exceed the cost of nudgeSize mints, pure-profit MEV returns'), now executed at 9.5× and 20,000×; nudgeSize (:106) constrains a COUNT, never a value. P3 'NFTs have no realizable path' ✗ DEAD — and this entry's OWN run-16 re-triage predicted it ('the acceptance invariant does NOT bound loss if the minted NFTs carry realizable value'); NFTMinterV2 is a plain ERC1155Supply with no transfer restriction and the units stake for phUSD (12.58 claimed in 30 days). P4 'minReward floor fully closes it' ✗ CONDITIONAL on an accepted wont-fix (ledger L-05 990d8c37…, default 0 = no floor); the contract's OWN NatSpec at :288-291 says the floor 'does NOT stop a front-runner from winning the pot; the floor only stops the loser from minting for less than they declared'. MITIGATION BOUNDED HONESTLY: P4 is not worthless — test_M01_minRewardsFloorDoesNotStopTheFrontRun shows that with a CORRECT floor set the loser's batch reverts and their capital IS spared. It is NARROWER than 'fully closed', not absent. Executed at HEAD: PoC_NudgeLineage_MevFrontrunNudge 2/2 PASS, PoC_NudgeLineage_M01PriceInflation 2/2 PASS — an honest user mints 5 REAL NFTs, pays 5,947.05 and receives 0 while a searcher with an outlay of 5,256.33 takes the 50,000 pot; second leg harms existing stakers at +252 bps rate and −780,595 s (−9 days) runway per 5-mint round, compounding on round two. PLAIN STATEMENT: the economic object the owner accepted on 2026-06-09 is not the economic object that exists at HEAD — the closure accepted 'an ordinary gas auction among real participants'; with P2 and P3 gone it is a gas auction over a PURE-PROFIT pot a bot can realize without ever intending to participate. ⚠ BOUNDING HONESTY (D-22): ZERO present on-chain exposure — 0 USDC / 0 USDS / 0 ETH on RatchetBatchNFTMinter, 0 at the block before the fix, batchMinter() repointed, no principal theft in any of the 11 tests. ⚠ COUPLED TO ledger L-05 990d8c37… (wont-fix): this closure DEPENDS on the mitigation L-05 declares default-off, so neither can be read alone — see WATCH-20-minrewards-frontend-obligation-unowned. ⚠ Leaving it `fixed` is wrong under EITHER reading; if the residual is still acceptable, re-close it with a rationale written against HEAD's premises. Record: reports/phoenix-nft-staking-20/findings/reopen/. ⚠ LABEL-COLLISION: run-20's own M-01 is fcaca002… — unrelated. [phoenix-nft-staking-21] RE-ANCHORED (contract/function only, STATUS UNCHANGED = fixed): src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:batchMint → src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:batchMint. BOTH — re-anchored to the new file; the lineage is equally present on the frozen, mainnet-deployed src/BatchNFTMinter.sol. **[phoenix-nft-staking-21, OPERATOR TRIAGE 2026-07-21]** STATUS: fixed -> wont-fix; humanReviewFlag CLEARED; reopen proposal RESOLVED. THE 2026-06-09 OWNER TRIAGE IS UPHELD, NOT OVERRIDDEN — the race outcome remains ACCEPTED protocol behaviour. What changed is the RATIONALE, for two reasons. (1) The reopen proposal's lead argument DOES NOT SURVIVE: it rebutted the claim that `minReward` 'fully closes' the front-run by quoting the NatSpec at :286-291 ('does NOT stop a front-runner from winning the pot'), but the 2026-06-09 triage NEVER MADE THAT CLAIM — it scoped `minReward` to honest-user OVERPAYMENT and separately and explicitly accepted 'the remaining race — who wins the pot among qualifying batches — is an accepted gas-auction among genuine protocol participants'. The NatSpec contradicts a claim nobody made. DO NOT RE-FILE ON THIS GROUND. (2) The ground that DOES survive is narrow and is now discharged: 'fully closed by minReward' was inaccurate because the floor is DEFAULT-OFF and story-022 widened it from a scalar to a per-token `minRewards[]` array — the front-end obligation that carries it is tracked at ledger L-05 990d8c37…, whose owner was UNNAMED until 2026-07-21 and is now the operator (protective UI). ECONOMIC CORRECTION, recorded so it is not re-derived: the 'honest-user overpayment' harm ASSUMES the loser paid the qualifying cost FOR THE POT. They did not — they paid it for the NFTs, which they receive REGARDLESS of who wins the race. Losing forfeits a bonus that mainnet numbers show is loss-making to chase (~634 USDS qualifying cost vs a ~94.95 USDC pot at block 25577241). Nobody batches 40 mints to farm a 95 USDC tip. ⚠ COUPLING (one watch covers both, but DO NOT COLLAPSE — two distinct defects, two distinct fixes, per D-29): this entry is the RACE (who wins among qualifying callers); 858e9e80… is the value-blind GATE (payout decoupled from outlay). The race's harm is CONDITIONAL on the gate becoming profitable — below the pot-vs-cost line there is no searcher at all. RE-RATE TO HIGH IMMEDIATELY on the shared arming relation: (a) nudge pot on 0x86866e01...029d exceeding ~634 USDS-equivalent (nudgeSize x current mint price); (b) nudge pot on 0x81896F48...A1C7 exceeding nudgeSize x 70.000000 USDC; (c) ANY reduction of nudgeSize or of the per-mint price — the relation inverts from EITHER side; (d) NudgeRatchet.batchMinter() (0x7A4eD111...) repointed such that the donation stream lands where the pot outgrows the qualifying cost; (e) deployment of src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol behind a value-forwarding dispatcher. Triggers (c)/(d) are ORDINARY operator moves = Law-3 footgun, in scope. ⚠ If the relation inverts while the L-05 front-end floor is not actually shipped, the honest claimant has NEITHER a profitable-race deterrent NOR an active slippage floor — that conjunction is the thing to watch. findings.label: L-05
findings.title: minReward==0 default silently opts out of the slippage guard
findings.note: NEW Low at run phoenix-nft-staking-14 (untriaged). Root cause: batchMint's minReward (story-015's slippage guard against M-01) defaults to 0 for backward compat; an integrating front-end that omits the param re-exposes M-01 in full. Integration footgun. Distinct from M-01 (this is the opt-out default of the mitigation, not the MEV race itself). [TRIAGE 2026-05-30] WONT-FIX at the contract level (user triage 2026-05-30). The minReward==0 default cannot be removed in-contract: legitimate non-nudge batches (count < nudgeSize) must pass minReward=0, so the contract cannot force a non-zero floor globally. INTEGRATION REQUIREMENT (carried forward, not dropped): user condition 1 ('a normal user never mints-and-gets-zero') holds ONLY if the front-end derives and passes a non-zero, pot-based minReward (AMM-slippage style) for every nudge-qualifying (count >= nudgeSize) batch. This obligation now lives at the integration/UI layer, not the contract. Closed as wont-fix on the contract; the front-end enforcement is the responsible owner of condition 1. [phoenix-nft-staking-19] Re-confirmed present @321d0a9 (cold-full, DEDUP-19-003 lineage); wont-fix preserved (authoritative human triage). lastSeenRun bumped to 19. [phoenix-nft-staking-20] ⚠ DISCLOSURE AGAINST AN ACCEPTED WONT-FIX (not an override; your 2026-05-30 triage stands). Two facts have emerged that the wont-fix did not anticipate. (1) **COUPLING**: ledger M-01's (521c20ad…) 2026-06-09 `fixed` DEPENDS on the very mitigation this entry declares DEFAULT-OFF — its premise P4 is 'the minReward floor fully closes it', while this entry's accepted position is that minReward defaults to 0 and the obligation now lives at the front-end. The two entries lean on each other and NEITHER CAN BE READ ALONE. The contract's own NatSpec at :288-291 further bounds P4: the floor 'does NOT stop a front-runner from winning the pot; the floor only stops the loser from minting for less than they declared' — i.e. the mitigation the M-01 closure called 'fully closed' is documented in-contract as PARTIAL. It is not worthless (test_M01_minRewardsFloorDoesNotStopTheFrontRun shows the loser's capital IS spared when a correct floor is set) — it is NARROWER than claimed. (2) **THE OBLIGATION WIDENED WITHOUT RE-TRIAGE**: this wont-fix transferred condition 1 ('a normal user never mints-and-gets-zero') to the front-end, which must derive and pass a non-zero, pot-based minReward for every nudge-qualifying batch. story-022 widened that from a SCALAR `minReward` to a PER-TOKEN `minRewards[]` ARRAY parallel to a caller-supplied `rewardTokens[]`, with 'Array hygiene is the caller's responsibility' (BatchNFTMinter.sol:258-266) — a materially larger integration obligation than the one that was accepted, and it was never re-triaged. **NOBODY HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED AS VERIFYING THE FRONT-END MEETS IT, AND NO RUN HAS EVER CHECKED.** Until an owner is named, M-01's P4 leg has no backing. See WATCH-20-minrewards-frontend-obligation-unowned. Executed consequence when unmet: an honest user mints 5 real NFTs, pays 5,947.05 and receives 0 (test/PoC_NudgeLineage_MevFrontrunNudge.t.sol, 2/2 PASS @0d1a0b2). [phoenix-nft-staking-21] RE-ANCHORED (contract/function only, STATUS UNCHANGED = wont-fix): src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:batchMint → src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:batchMint (minRewards[] zero-default opt-out). ⚠ RELOCATION OF A WONT-FIX — SUPPRESSION BOUNDARY. BOTH files. The owner’s acceptance was granted against the NARROWER design (the OWNER pins ONE payout asset). On the sibling, ANY qualifying CALLER names ANY ERC20 the contract holds (FORK-PARITY §B4.1). DO NOT auto-suppress the class on the sibling under the old triage (DS-05). Also §B4.2: rescueERC20 degraded from "the missing escape hatch" (frozen :173-180) to "NOT a reliable escape hatch … a race the owner will usually lose" (sibling :191-201) — a reduction in owner recourse the prior triage did not contemplate. **[phoenix-nft-staking-21, OPERATOR RE-TRIAGE 2026-07-21]** WONT-FIX RE-AFFIRMED, NOW AGAINST THE WIDENED SURFACE — this discharges the run-20 disclosure and WATCH-20-minrewards-frontend-obligation-unowned. The 2026-05-30 acceptance transferred condition 1 ('a normal user never mints-and-gets-zero') to the front-end but NAMED NO OWNER; run-20 flagged that story-022 widened the obligation from a SCALAR minReward to a PER-TOKEN minRewards[] array parallel to caller-supplied rewardTokens[], and that no run had ever verified it. ⚠ OWNER NOW IDENTIFIED: the OPERATOR owns the front-end obligation and will ship a protective UI that derives and passes a non-zero, pot-based minRewards[] for every nudge-qualifying (count >= nudgeSize) batch. The operator has re-accepted EXPLICITLY AGAINST THE WIDER ARRAY-SHAPED DESIGN, which is precisely what DS-05 required before the class could be treated as accepted on the sibling — DS-05 is therefore DISCHARGED for this entry (it was NOT auto-suppressed under the old narrower triage). BASIS FOR WONT-FIX: a caller who bypasses the protective UI harms ONLY THEIR OWN CAPITAL (mint-and-get-zero, or a mis-shaped array). Verified this run that the blast radius is self-contained: duplicate rewardTokens entries fail closed on the second safeTransfer; a fake/non-ERC20 token only defeats that same caller's own minRewards floor and moves no real value; the payment-token exclusion runs UNCONDITIONALLY on every element before any funds move; the balanceOf read leg is a STATICCALL (_snapshotRewards is `private view`) and the payout leg is nonReentrant with the minter approval already revoked. No other user and no protocol funds are exposed => C4 known-invalid 'user input mistakes'. ⚠ NOT COVERED BY THE UI, carried forward separately: run-21 §B4.2 recorded that rescueERC20 degraded from 'the missing escape hatch' (frozen :173-180) to 'NOT a reliable escape hatch … a race the owner will usually lose' (sibling :191-201). That is a reduction in OWNER RECOURSE, not a caller-side input obligation, and a protective front-end does nothing for it. ⚠ VERIFICATION GAP REMAINS OPEN BY DESIGN: no run has inspected the front-end, and the UI is stated as intended, not shipped. This entry is the record of who owns it; it is not evidence the UI exists. **[CORRECTION 2026-07-21, same day]** ⚠ ERRATUM AGAINST THE 2026-07-21 RE-TRIAGE BLOCK ABOVE. That block listed, as part of the wont-fix supporting facts, the claim that 'duplicate rewardTokens entries fail closed on the second safeTransfer'. THAT CLAIM IS FALSE AS WRITTEN and is hereby STRUCK. It was taken from the contract's own NatSpec (:258-266, :412-415, 'harming only the careless caller') and not verified against executed evidence. THE TRUTH: `_snapshotRewards` reads balanceOf PER LISTED ENTRY, so a token listed twice snapshots the prior pot P twice. `_payRewards` pays P (leaving the batch's own in-loop donations D), then pays P again — which SUCCEEDS whenever D >= P. The caller takes 2P, the second P funded from THEIR OWN BATCH'S DONATIONS, which the snapshot-before-loop design (:326-344, :390-399) reserves for the NEXT claimant. The victim is therefore the next honest batcher and the incentive budget — NOT the duplicate-lister's own capital. It is NOT caller self-harm and MUST NOT be triaged as array hygiene. Run-21 executed evidence: invariant_nudgeSolvency and invariant_nudgeNoSelfFund BOTH BROKEN across cold corpora, and PoC_DuplicateRewardWithDonations PASS (paid 30,000,000 against prePot 15,000,000; second corpus 36,000,000 against 18,000,000). This defect is tracked SEPARATELY as ledger a62fe01a25e28fe7c327b65728e15408017525d9611a92d3363b7066c6c437ad (label M-02, status OPEN, Medium) — ⚠ DO NOT CITE THIS L-05 ENTRY, OR THE NATSPEC DUPLICATE PARAGRAPH, AS A BASIS FOR SUPPRESSING IT. Fix plan: docs/phoenix-nft-staking-duplicate-reward-token-dedupe-plan.md. SCOPE OF THE ERRATUM: this corrects ONE supporting fact only. L-05's wont-fix DISPOSITION STANDS UNCHANGED — its actual subject is the minReward==0 default-off slippage floor, whose harm genuinely is the bypassing caller's own capital, and its other supporting facts are unaffected and re-verified: a fake/non-ERC20 token defeats only that same caller's own minRewards floor and moves no real value; the payment-token exclusion runs unconditionally on every element before any funds move; the balanceOf read leg is a STATICCALL (_snapshotRewards is `private view`); the payout leg is nonReentrant with the minter approval already revoked. GENERAL LESSON, recorded deliberately: a NatSpec safety claim is not proof. Both this duplicate claim and the nudge's 'by construction' bound (L-04 / F-20-07 a7dffb34…) are asserted in comments and backed by NO CODE. Verify against source plus executed evidence before using either to close a finding.

findings.title: emergencyWithdraw skips _recomputeSchedule/_updatePool, leaving stale rewardRate that over-emits the reward budget to surviving stakers
findings.humanReviewFlag: ⚠ DISCLOSURE (run-20): wont-fix premise (b) falsified on copy #4. Owner triage UNCHANGED pending re-read.
findings.note: NEW Medium at run phoenix-nft-staking-16 (cold --full re-scan of HEAD 5f863d2). emergencyWithdraw decrements totalStaked but skips _updatePool/_recomputeSchedule and never advances lastRewardTime, so the next _updatePool over-emits the reward budget to survivors by oldTotal/newTotal (100x). Solvency invariant holds throughout (over-draw clamped to rewardBudget at NFTStaker.sol:329) => value-leak / runway drain, NOT insolvency or principal theft. Violates the M-03 'no participation multiplier' Critical Invariant => cross-referenced as spec-conformance F-01 (carries the LIVE Medium per Law 1; NOT collapsed into QA noise). Submission-grade PoC validated PASS (2/2) by poc-validator against unmodified src @ 5f863d2 (workspace/phoenix-nft-staking/test/poc-M02-EmergencyWithdrawOverEmission.t.sol: test_M02_emergencyWithdraw_inflatesSurvivorEmission, test_M02_selfProfit_recoverPrincipalThenSidecarDrains; written GREEN). report-writer emitted the H/M submission; reportPath set. [TRIAGE 2026-06-09] Owner triage (2026-06-09): ACKNOWLEDGED / WON'T-FIX. NFTStaker is deployed and non-upgradeable; the only code fix (the pure-arithmetic rewardRate resize inside emergencyWithdraw) would require redeploying NFTStaker and migrating existing stakers to the new contract. NFTStaker exposes NO migrate-on-behalf mechanism — every position-moving entrypoint (stake/unstake/claim/emergencyWithdraw) is keyed to msg.sender; there is no depositFor / migrator role / batch — so a migration would force every staker to self-exit and re-stake. Owner accepts the residual over-emission rather than force a migration. Operational mitigation (recorded as the basis for won't-fix): the stale-rate window is closable on demand — the owner monitors EmergencyWithdrawn events and calls pullAndRefresh() (onlyOwner; triggers _recomputeSchedule, resizing rewardRate to current totalStaked) promptly after any emergency exit, bounding the leak to the owner's reaction gap; any stake/unstake/claim/topUp/setTargetAPY also resizes the rate. findings.title: InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator immutable stakedId lacks live-parity assertion vs staker.stakedId() — deploy-time mis-wire AND post-deploy setStakedId drift strands
findings.note: NEW Low at run phoenix-nft-staking-18 (story-019, new InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator). Constructor wires source/destination stakers without asserting stakedId/stakedToken consistency; an owner mis-wire can strand principal parked in the migrator mid-migration. Law-3 non-obvious deploy-time configuration footgun (in scope); no attacker, no theft, avoidable with a correct deploy. Bundled in QA report. Recommend a constructor cross-check asserting stakedToken/stakedId parity across the wired stakers. [phoenix-nft-staking-19 CONSOLIDATION — DEDUP-19-004 second strand, no new label/fingerprint] Root cause is one bug — the migrator's immutable stakedId carries no LIVE-parity assertion against the staker's owner-mutable stakedId(). Run-18 L-01 = the DEPLOY-TIME mis-wire strand. DEDUP-19-004 = the DYNAMIC POST-DEPLOY strand: a legitimate setStakedId reissue (onlyOwner + totalStaked==0-gated, i.e. only after users are parked) drifts staker.stakedId()->newId while migrator.stakedId stays oldId. CORRECTED IMPACT (supersedes the code-scanner's inverted narrative; per reports/phoenix-nft-staking-19/L-01-corrected-adjudication.md, severity-auditor source-traced): the physically-parked ERC1155 units are oldId and migrator.stakedId==oldId stays aligned with them forever, so claimTimedOut (transfers migrator.stakedId=oldId) STILL WORKS — the permissionless escape hatch is INTACT — and rescueERC1155's totalParked floor (balanceOf(this,migrator.stakedId)=balanceOf(oldId)) STILL guards the correct balance — the floor is INTACT. The ONLY real consequence is that migrateIn -> staker.depositFor pulls stakedToken.safeTransferFrom(migrator, staker, staker.stakedId()=newId) from a migrator holding only oldId -> REVERTS, so owner migrateIn re-injection BRICKS. Fully recoverable: parked users self-rescue via the permissionless claimTimedOut after migrationTimeout (1–30 days). No theft, no permanent loss, no floor void, no hatch kill -> stays LOW. CORRECTED REMEDIATION: assert migrator.stakedId == staker.stakedId() at the ENTRY of migrateIn (fail-loud before the re-injection loop), OR block setStakedId while totalParked>0 at the migrator. DO NOT repoint claimTimedOut/rescueERC1155 to read staker.stakedId() — that would BREAK the currently-working hatch/floor (migrator holds oldId, not newId). INCOMPLETE-FIX / RE-AUDIT TRAP (recorded, see WATCH-19-L01-incomplete-fix-trap): run-18 L-01's constructor-only cross-check does NOT close this dynamic strand (it passes at deploy then drifts on a later setStakedId); a constructor-only patch MUST NOT be auto-flipped to fixed — verify a live parity assert at migrateIn (or a totalParked>0 reissue guard) before flipping. NON-OBVIOUS Law-3 footgun: the safe threshold silently migrates from per-token to whitelist-aggregate. ⚠ MEDIUM-ESCALATION TRIGGER (proposal P5): re-rate to Medium the moment any live/pending deployment funds the whitelist so SUM(pot_i) approaches/exceeds nudgeSize*mintPrice — the AGGREGATE re-expression of the 858e9e80/521c20ad reopen triggers (a)-(e), evaluated on the whitelist-aggregate, never per token. ⚠ REFILE DISCLOSURE (disclose-when-re-filing-an-owner-wontfix): related to ledger H-01 858e9e807abee888… (wont-fix, operator triage 2026-07-21) + companion M-01 521c20ad… (wont-fix). OWNER CORRECTION 2026-07-26 (funding source): across the Phoenix suite the protocol OWNS its capital and earns YIELD on it from external vaults (e.g. Tokemak); that yield funds phlimbo and the batchMinter nudge pot. The pot is yield on protocol-owned principal - NEVER principal itself, NEVER user deposits. Over-topping the pot is therefore OPPORTUNITY COST (the yield could have gone straight into liquidity growth), NOT ECONOMIC LOSS. It is an accepted short-run cost and a deliberate MARKETING SPEND: a visible profit opportunity pulls users in, and the deficit closes as the lowest-bidding marginal user snipes the mint. NudgeStreamer meters release precisely so the market finds a clearing price - a LARGE POT IS THE MECHANISM WORKING, not a failure. EMPIRICAL: in live operation the pot has NEVER ONCE reached even 50% of the qualifying cost before someone minted. Recorded in registered-projects.json as systemAssumptions 'NUDGE-POT FUNDING SOURCE', designDecisions 'Nudge pot size is a SUBSIDY RATE, not an invariant', and knownIssues KI #16. Because a pot exceeding the qualifying cost is a deliberate subsidy rate rather than a value leak, the run-25 re-weigh has no basis. findings.note: [phoenix-nft-staking-22] NEW (DEDUP-22-002, pattern-matcher PATTERN-MR-002 + contract-profiler BMT-LOCAL-01). Owner remove via setNudgeTokenWhitelist(token,false) is swap-and-pop (LAST token moves into the removed slot), so getNudgeTokens() ordering changes; a caller who fetched the order before the reorder submits batchMint with a positional minRewards[] now mapped to the wrong tokens — stale minRewards[i] compared against a different token's snapshot => spurious revert (self-DoS) or a floor silently protecting the wrong token. NO ASSET IMPACT: minRewards[] is a FLOOR only, the whole prior pot is paid regardless; CODE-VER-07 confirms index integrity + length checks (no OOB, no wrong-token payout). Law-3 non-obvious owner/caller ordering footgun. KEPT DISTINCT from ledger L-05 990d8c37 (wont-fix) and Q-01 cabd4a3d (open) per dedup — different root cause, do not collapse. Safe config: callers/UI must re-fetch getNudgeTokens() immediately before every batchMint (already in NatSpec); consider a token-keyed minRewards mapping or expected-ordering hash so positional drift fails closed. *** RE-FILE DISCLOSURE (disclose-when-refiling-owner-wontfix) - THIS ENTRY DOES NOT OVERRIDE ANY WONT-FIX. *** Prior entries NAMED: 43e8c48626ee74b51d538bd9ed12bf4898b976818f6fb44fea844ff3757daefe (M-01, wont-fix) and 858e9e807abee888b378db210bae982f23fe7b5d91052321e204d7ba568579b7 (H-01, wont-fix). RE-ARM trigger unchanged: re-rate the moment a live/pending deployment funds the whitelist so Sigma(pot_i) approaches/exceeds one qualifying cost.'; 858e9e80 - 'THE 6.7x MARGIN IS REAL', RE-RATE triggers (b) 'nudge pot ... exceeding nudgeSize x 70.000000 USDC' and (e) 'deployment of src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol behind any value-forwarding dispatcher.' RE-FILE BASIS: both Sigma figures were computed over a pot set that STRUCTURALLY EXCLUDED the payment token, because at triage time _snapshotRewards skipped it at runtime. Story-029 deleted that skip and ADDED A POOL TO Sigma, so the prior arithmetic is not a statement about 5015f1b. Root-cause class changed (_snapshotRewards scope, not the gate) => new fingerprint. Both prior wont-fixes STAND UNTOUCHED - their own re-arm triggers (b) and (e) are MET, not bypassed (NudgeRatchet IS a value-forwarding dispatcher). This entry supplies only the delta.

KI #15 does NOT suppress this: excluded by KI #15's own carve-out (d), 'the aggregate over-funding class ... which is about the pot being too LARGE relative to cost'. This finding does NOT assert 'batching is profitable', 'the pot is sniped by MEV bots', 'payment token should not be whitelisted as a nudge token', or 'setNudgeTokenWhitelist no longer rejects the payment token' - none of those may be reintroduced into the writeup. Law 3 does not suppress either: docs/multi-token-nudge.md §4.1 AFFIRMATIVELY BLESSES the collision configuration as 'permitted and safe, not forbidden', so an owner following the project's own documentation is not making an admin mistake. Story-faithfulness F-25-01: the implementation is FAITHFUL to commit 0318089 §3.2; the defect is in the STORY'S OWN JUSTIFICATION (Law 1 over Law 2 - an unsafe intent is escalated, not blessed). M-02's ledger entry is retained with status `merged` (no silent drop); its mechanism, PoC and safe-config text stay readable there. Rationale: M-02 has zero standalone impact - fix M-01 and the recycling is a wash; fix M-02 and M-01 still drains the pot.

*** CORRECTED CROSS-REPO CITATION - THE PRIOR SOURCE WAS STALE. *** The recycling mechanism was originally sourced from lib/phoenix-nft-staking's NESTED pin lib/mutable/yield-claim-nft @ aa86be6, where NudgeRatchet._dispatch ended in `IERC20(_token).safeTransfer(batchMinter, bal)` at :100. THAT LINE NO LONGER EXISTS. The authoritative source is the TOP-LEVEL submodule lib/yield-claim-nft @ **d4cc563**, where the :100 safeTransfer is **DELETED** and replaced by `forceApprove(streamer, bal); collectNudge(batchMinter, _token, bal)` at **:156-161**. Any writeup or re-verification MUST cite d4cc563 :156-161, never aa86be6 :100.

**CONCLUSION SURVIVES, BUT IS METERED, NOT INSTANTANEOUS.** Verified against d4cc563 that NudgeStreamer is VALUE-CONSERVING: no fee, burn, skim or retention anywhere in _settle (NudgeStreamer.sol:182-190); _accrued (:195-200) caps the released amount at `buffer`, which prevents OVER-transfer but never WITHHOLDS value; and BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.batchMint:530 calls pullPendingStream BEFORE the :535 snapshot, so streamed value is in the pot when the pot is measured. Therefore the STEADY STATE IS NUMERICALLY UNCHANGED by conservation - 100% of C still returns to the pot. What changes is the COST PROFILE, and these are NEW attacker costs the run-25 writeup did not charge: (i) recovery of C is LINEAR OVER `duration`, not atomic; (ii) one full C is PERMANENTLY ESCROWED IN-FLIGHT in the streamer (the loop never fully drains); (iii) the attack becomes an INTERRUPTIBLE MULTI-DAY RACE rather than a single transaction - the owner or a competing minter can act inside the window; and (iv) a **FOURTH ARMING CONDITION** now exists on top of the three already recorded: the streamer path must be COMPLETELY wired - token whitelisted AND `registerStream` called AND `setNudgeStreamer` set - because the unset / NotRegistered / NotWhitelisted paths HARD-REVERT batchMint. An unwired or partially wired streamer does not degrade the attack, it BLOCKS the mint outright.

**UNPINNED SEVERITY PARAMETER: `duration`.** The recovery period is a `registerStream` ARGUMENT, not a source constant, so it is NOT DISCOVERABLE FROM SOURCE and this run COULD NOT RESOLVE IT. Severity of the Leg-2 repeatability is a function of it: a short duration approaches the original atomic claim, a long duration makes the loop slow, capital-intensive and easily interrupted. Resolve `duration` from the live registerStream call before finalising Leg-2 severity; it is recorded in openGaps (asOfRun phoenix-nft-staking-25).

The pot is yield on protocol-owned principal - NEVER principal itself, NEVER user deposits. Over-topping the pot is therefore OPPORTUNITY COST (the yield could have gone straight into liquidity growth), NOT ECONOMIC LOSS. It is an accepted short-run cost and a deliberate MARKETING SPEND: a visible profit opportunity pulls users in, and the deficit closes as the lowest-bidding marginal user snipes the mint. NudgeStreamer meters release precisely so the market finds a clearing price - a LARGE POT IS THE MECHANISM WORKING, not a failure. EMPIRICAL: in live operation the pot has NEVER ONCE reached even 50% of the qualifying cost before someone minted. Applied to this finding: the count-only gate paying the accumulated pot to a QUALIFYING batcher IS THE MECHANISM, not a defect - story-029's deletion of the _snapshotRewards payment-token skip widened what the (intended) gate can release, and the release itself is the intended subsidy. The 4.00x Sigma/C figure and the +150.000000 USDC PoC measure the SUBSIDY RATE, not a loss: the 150 USDC is externally-derived yield spent on customer acquisition, and the claimant paid for nudgeSize real mints to get it. NOTHING REMAINS BENEATH THIS FINDING: the three genuine-defect tests - (a) pot leaving WITHOUT the caller paying for nudgeSize real mints, (b) refund > paymentAmount, (c) a NON-QUALIFYING batch extracting pot-sized value (KI #15 carve-outs (a)/(b)/(c)) - were ALL VERIFIED CLEAN by run-25. *** RUN-25 MIS-READ KI #15 CARVE-OUT (d). *** Run-25 treated (d) 'aggregate over-funding' as leaving this finding outside KI #15. [phoenix-nft-staking-25] NEW MEDIUM @5015f1b (DEDUP-25-02). batchMint steps 6+7 pay `price` to NFTMinterV2._executeMint, which safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, config.dispatcher, price); NudgeRatchet._dispatch (lib/mutable/yield-claim-nft/src/dispatchers/NudgeRatchet.sol:83-101, transfer at :100) then does IERC20(_token).safeTransfer(batchMinter, bal) - 100% OF BALANCE, per its own NatSpec 'DESIGN: this sweeps the FULL token balance, not the `amount` argument.' A competent, non-malicious owner would be SURPRISED that the batch minter paying its mints through the dispatcher that funds its own pot creates a closed loop. No malicious-owner vector is asserted. CROSS-REPO ASSUMPTION STATED HONESTLY: both legs were read AT SOURCE; NEITHER was verified against a live deployment - the ledger records the current mainnet wiring as repointed and the pot as empty. findings.label: L-03
findings.title: Budget/charge lockstep is a silent cross-repo invariant; live `price` allowance stands across two callbacks
findings.severityNote: Low (watch-note) - NOT a bug today. Confidence: medium as a hazard; the escape is verified sound at 5015f1b. ** THIS ENTRY IS ONE OF THE TWO CONDITIONS ON THE ad36260f `fixed` PROPOSAL. **
findings.note:
[phoenix-nft-staking-25] NEW LOW / WATCH-NOTE @5015f1b (DEDUP-25-06). The outflow leg at :624-626 is QUOTED, NOT MEASURED (`budget -= price` at :625), the deliberate inverse of the inbound bracket at :577-579. Correctness rests on a property of a DIFFERENT REPOSITORY: NFTMinterV2._executeMint debiting this contract exactly config.price, exactly once, per mint - verified at source (yield-claim-nft/src/NFTMinterV2.sol:183, the SOLE transferFrom in the file), holds today including under the standard fee-on-transfer model. THE HAZARD IS HOW INVISIBLE ITS FAILURE WOULD BE: _executeMint makes TWO external calls after the debit and before returning - ATokenDispatcherV2.dispatch (:191) and _mint (:196, firing onERC1155Received on a CALLER-CHOSEN recipient) - and with a payment token that does not decrement allowance on transferFrom, the forceApprove(minter, price) at :624 IS STILL STANDING during both. Unexploitable today for ONE reason only: the minter's single transferFrom sources msg.sender. Any future mintOnBehalf(address from, ...), batching inside _executeMint, or a second charge would immediately RE-OPEN ad36260f against P, WITH NO LOCAL SIGNAL in phoenix-nft-staking - `budget` would simply be wrong rather than reverting.

NM-02 escape confirmed at source - THIN MARGIN. Three independent reasons must ALL continue to hold: (1) nonReentrant at :464 blocks re-entering batchMint; (2) `budget -= price` executes BEFORE the mint, so the hook cannot observe an un-decremented budget (CEI holds within the iteration); (3) the standing allowance is exactly one mint's price and is spender-locked. THE MARGIN ON (2) AND (3) IS THIN - moving the decrement after the mint, or widening the approval, makes this LIVE. THE PER-ITERATION ABSOLUTE APPROVAL IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT A COSMETIC TIDY-UP. Suppression under KI #1 CONSIDERED AND DECLINED (Law-3 exception: composes two settings that are each the contract's designed purpose; non-obvious => footgun => in scope). RECOMMENDATION: measure the outflow leg (a balanceOf bracket around the single mint - a legitimate narrow bracket by the file's own :597-599 rule, PROVIDED the payment token is not itself donated back as D inside the same call, which it may be, so this is not free), or add an explicit post-loop assertion that the aggregate debit equals Sigma price. FILED SO THE ad36260f `fixed` PROPOSAL IS NOT READ AS UNCONDITIONAL.

findings.label: Q-01
findings.title: The `available` cap cannot do what its comment says it does; carries the merged DEDUP-25-09 residual and P-04's DoS tail
findings.severityNote: QA. Impact today: NONE (provably non-binding). Confidence: high that the claim is false; not currently exploitable.
findings.note:
[phoenix-nft-staking-25] NEW QA @5015f1b (DEDUP-25-08). The comment at :647-655 retains the cap 'only so an unforeseen shortfall degrades into a smaller refund rather than a revert.' It cannot serve that purpose: `available` is an ABSOLUTE balanceOf and equals P + (credited - C) + D, so a shortfall in the caller's own credit does not make it bind until P AND this batch's donations D have already been consumed in full. IN EXACTLY THE SCENARIO THE COMMENT NAMES, THE SHORTFALL IS SILENTLY ABSORBED BY THE POT INSTEAD OF DEGRADING THE REFUND. A cap doing what the prose claims would have to be caller-scoped, and no such quantity is tracked after :581. Provably non-binding today: budget <= credited (:580 min) and available = P + (credited - C) + D >= credited - C >= budget, so refund == budget on every constructible path - dead code that reads as a safety net.

*** MERGED RESIDUAL FROM THE SUPPRESSED DEDUP-25-09 (sanitizer §2 - preserved, NOT dropped): *** `budget` is a ONE-SHOT MEASUREMENT PINNED ONCE AT :581 AND NEVER RE-VALIDATED, so ANY post-:581 erosion of this contract's payment-token holdings is charged to P, silently. This needs NO weird token - P-03 ranks a negative-rebase prime token as an independent mechanism. *** P-04's DoS TAIL RIDES HERE TOO: *** once such erosion exceeds P + D, the step-9/10 swap turns a silent pot shrink into a batchMint REVERT ON THE PAYOUT LEG. The C4 known-invalid rule invalidated DEDUP-25-09's WEIRD-TOKEN EXPLOIT NARRATIVE, not this UNRECONCILED-MEASUREMENT RESIDUAL. Filed because the residual is the same balanceOf conflation story-029 was written to eliminate, sitting at the one site the file elsewhere explicitly forbids absolute reads (:585-605), with a comment that would mislead the next author into believing a protection exists. RECOMMENDATION: delete the cap and let an impossible shortfall revert honestly, or track a caller-scoped quantity and cap on that.

findings.title: Unisolated cross-contract flush loop can brick batchMint (availability/isolation leg only)
findings.note:
[phoenix-nft-staking-26] NEW @9611312 (D-26-01). Merges LOCAL-NS-01 (consequence limb) + S-01 + PATTERN-001 + CODE-01. The flush loop at :531-534 (block :528-536) iterates the OWNER's nudge-token whitelist calling NudgeStreamer.pullPendingStream with no try/catch and WITHOUT gating on `qualifies`; a revert inside the streamer (src/NudgeStreamer.sol:243 via pullPendingStream:224) rolls back the whole mint. The new increment: non-qualifying batches LOST THEIR STRUCTURAL IMMUNITY (_snapshotRewards:801 short-circuits balanceOf behind `qualifies`, _payRewards:831 skips zero amounts), so a `count < nudgeSize` caller now has exposure for ZERO benefit. *** LEG B IS KILLED - do NOT restate it as a mechanism. *** No plain-ERC20 path to an over-stated sum(buffer_i) exists; every enumerated mechanism is token-side (negative rebase, burn-on-hold, clawback, blacklist-zeroing) and C4-invalid standalone. findings.note: [phoenix-nft-staking-26] NEW @9611312 (D-26-08, from PATTERN-002). NOT present in this project's ledger before. setNudgeStreamer (:297-300) accepts any address with no structural probe. ASYMMETRIC WITH ITS COUNTERPARTY: NudgeStreamer.registerStream deliberately probes the batchMinter with isNudgeToken (:127, documented :10-17) to confirm the target type; the reverse direction has no equivalent check. AGGRAVATING: the event is emitted BEFORE assignment (:298-299), so a mis-point reads as a clean success in logs. The reachable residual is a CONTRACT WITH A PERMISSIVE FALLBACK (a Safe, a proxy with an unset implementation, another Phoenix contract): the flush then succeeds and does nothing, forever, while donor buffers accumulate unreachably. HELD AT LOW despite genuine Medium-class cross-project precedent, on a SUBSTANTIVE DISTINCTION: there the brick sat on a VALUE-BEARING path; here it degrades an OPTIONAL INCENTIVE whose funds remain in protocol custody, keep accumulating on the correctly-pointed streamer, and flush normally once the pointer is fixed - fully recoverable, no value lost. Likelihood limb also weak (EOA case defeated). FIX: probe the target structurally before assignment (mirror registerStream); emit the event AFTER assignment. findings.label: L-06 / F-04-030
findings.title: story-030 left an unenforced ordering guarantee standing inside the comment block it rewrote, and its own new text contradicts it
findings.note:
[phoenix-nft-staking-26] NEW @9611312 (D-26-11, from F-01). *** DUAL-ROUTED TO BOTH L-06 (QA bundle) AND F-04-030 (spec-conformance.md). ONE LEDGER ENTRY, ONE FINGERPRINT, TWO CHANNELS - INTENTIONAL per upstream decision 3, NOT A DUPLICATE. Do not dedup either channel away. *** The block at :659-665 (claim 2, 'and vice versa') asserts a SYMMETRIC mutual-non-interference guarantee and attributes it to ORDERING. NEITHER HALF SURVIVES: independence comes from SOURCING (`budget` vs `snapshot`), not sequence; and in the one case where ordering binds (erosion between step 5 and step 9), refund-first charges the shortfall to D then P - so 'a refund funded out of a payout that is owed' is what the ordering CAUSES, not what it prevents. story-030's own Anchor E addition 20 lines below (:695-700, 'charged to the pot, silently') states the contradicting fact. In scope despite sitting outside the anchor's enumerated line range, because story-030's own review pass (:375-378) explicitly disowns 'it wasn't in my anchor list' as a defence. *** ESCALATION QUESTION Q1 ANSWERED: NO. *** The step-5 -> step-9 erosion path is NOT reachable without a token-side property (a negative rebase, an admin clawback/burn on a third party's instruction, or a FoT variant debiting sender price+fee) - all C4-invalid standalone; the contract's own comment at :700-701 names the first. PROOF on a plain 18-dp ERC20: (1) budget <= credited via min at :604; (2) the loop's decrement EQUALS its outflow exactly - batchMint:646 reads `price` from configs(_dispatcherIndex), :649 decrements by exactly that, and NFTMinterV2._executeMint (yield-claim-nft @ d4cc563, :179-183) reads `uint256 price = config.price` and safeTransferFrom's it - SAME STORAGE SLOT, SAME TRANSACTION, NO interleaving write; the price ramp at :188 happens AFTER the transfer; (3) no other outflow exists (pull :581 inbound, forceApprove :648/:655 balance-neutral, refund :711; rescueERC20 :386-388 is onlyOwner and cannot interleave under nonReentrant; the dispatcher sweeps ITS OWN balance; the streamer hop moves funds IN); (4) therefore available = P + (credited - C) + D and refund = budget <= credited - C <= available, so the `available` cap at :709 NEVER BINDS and no shortfall is charged to D or P. KI #16 CARVE-OUT FLAG FORMALLY DISCHARGED: (b) 'any path where refund > paymentAmount' is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE (refund <= budget <= paymentAmount by construction at :604, budget only decreases, totalPaid at :712 cannot underflow); (d) 'ANY CLAIMANT TAKING OTHER USERS' MONEY' DOES NOT FIRE (no claimant absorbs D or P on a plain token; there is no value transfer to classify). PINNED AT LOW, not QA: the defect is a false SAFETY guarantee on a load-bearing property and it is dual-routed to spec-conformance; that belongs in the Low band, not the discretionary-drop band. *** WATCH-26-02 - THE DOOR STAYS OPEN (Law 1). *** The structural-impossibility proof rests on leg (2), an UNDOCUMENTED CROSS-REPO config.price COUPLING (batchMint:646 <-> NFTMinterV2._executeMint:179-183 @ yield-claim-nft d4cc563). If NFTMinterV2 is ever changed so the amount charged is not the config.price the batchMinter read - a consumption-side fee, a two-pull mint, a price write before the transfer - then budget under-decrements, the erosion becomes reachable ON A PLAIN TOKEN, carve-out (d) FIRES, and THIS BECOMES A REAL VALUE-TRANSFER FINDING at MEDIUM OR HIGH. FIX: correct :659-665 to attribute independence to SOURCING not sequence, reconcile with the Anchor E text at :695-702, and DOCUMENT the cross-repo config.price coupling on the phoenix side - it is load-bearing and currently unstated. DISCLOSURE OWED: DISC-26-08 (in-source-overclaim cluster now has SEVEN live members; all different sites/claims - keep separate).

[2026-07-30 closeout - SEVERITY-AUDIT CORRECTION APPLIED] *** DISCRIMINATOR vs e16a9cac... (Q-01 / and its faithfulness twin c4c09ae3 F-01-031). DO NOT COLLAPSE. *** THIS ENTRY IS THE 'UNDOCUMENTED CROSS-REPO COUPLING + IN-FILE SELF-CONTRADICTION' case: the asserted property is FALSE (both halves of claim 2 fail -- independence comes from SOURCING not sequence, and the ordering CAUSES the very thing the comment claims it prevents), the file REFUTES ITSELF 20 lines below at :695-702 (story-030's own Anchor E, 'charged to the pot, silently'), and the property's real safety rests on an UNDISCLOSED CROSS-REPO COUPLING to NFTMinterV2._executeMint @ yield-claim-nft d4cc563 (WATCH-26-02). e16a9cac (Q-01) is the 'MACHINE-PROVED + LOCALLY SELF-CONSISTENT' case: a TRUE property (Halmos-proved at 2 streams, no fuzz counterexample), locally consistent, token-independent, with only its CITED BASIS wrong. REMEDIATIONS DIFFER: this entry needs the false claim deleted/corrected AND the external dependency documented; e16a9cac needs a basis restated. ownerCorrections.summary: OWNER CORRECTION 2026-07-26 (funding source): across the Phoenix suite the protocol OWNS its capital and earns YIELD on it from external vaults (e.g. Tokemak); that yield funds phlimbo and the batchMinter nudge pot. The pot is yield on protocol-owned principal - NEVER principal itself, NEVER user deposits. Over-topping the pot is therefore OPPORTUNITY COST (the yield could have gone straight into liquidity growth), NOT ECONOMIC LOSS. It is an accepted short-run cost and a deliberate MARKETING SPEND: a visible profit opportunity pulls users in, and the deficit closes as the lowest-bidding marginal user snipes the mint. NudgeStreamer meters release precisely so the market finds a clearing price - a LARGE POT IS THE MECHANISM WORKING, not a failure. EMPIRICAL: in live operation the pot has NEVER ONCE reached even 50% of the qualifying cost before someone minted. Recorded in registered-projects.json as systemAssumptions 'NUDGE-POT FUNDING SOURCE', designDecisions 'Nudge pot size is a SUBSIDY RATE, not an invariant', and knownIssues KI #16.
